cases.request: Assess whether SYNBANK's latest growth proves a stronger underwriting moat and give a useful next check for a public retail investor.
evidence: Synthetic issuer release R1, quarter ended 2026-06-30, table 2: revenue grew 30%; interest rates rose; customer/product mix changed.
Synthetic call C1 segment 18, CFO: Our proprietary underwriting is superior. No vintage-level losses or model comparisons were disclosed.
R1 table 4 discloses aggregate delinquency and credit-loss expense. Comparative definitions are unchanged. No private customer data is available.
expected: Separate management claim and growth outcome from proof of underwriting mechanism; consider rates and mix as alternative causes.
Describe the underwriting advantage as unproven from supplied public evidence, not a failed moat.
Use the next issuer release's aggregate delinquency/credit-loss disclosures as a limited proxy; identify the limitation and consequence without invented thresholds or private cohort homework.
cases.held_out_request: Can we infer a durable credit-selection edge from this quarter? Tell me what I could actually verify using public disclosures.

Segment 45, CFO: Mix added two percentage points and pricing added one. Segment 46, CEO: We are not disclosing retention figures. No other retention response occurs.
expected: Recover all response/follow-up turns before classifying components.
Margin drivers and quantification were answered, including later response; retention figures were explicitly declined, leaving improvement unresolved.
Cite segment locators and report the material gap neutrally; do not infer deception or poor retention from the refusal.

cases.request: Build the ten-year revenue assumptions for SYNADS and tell me which assumptions decide the result.
evidence: Synthetic filings F1-F3, MD&A table 5: ad revenue grew 8%, 12% and 13% in fiscal 2024-2026. The issuer reports paid clicks change (+7%, +5%, +6%) and cost-per-click change (+1%, +7%, +7%) for the same years, admitted through the fact resolver.

The issuer does not disclose query volume or market share. Synthetic panel P1 (publisher PanelCo, 2026-10-01, web and app sessions, publisher states +/- 20%) estimates share fell from 81% to 76% in fifteen months. Synthetic call C9 segment 12, CEO: query growth was the fastest in five years.
Consensus revenue growth for fiscal 2027 is 11%. A second line, partner network revenue, is 8% of revenue and flat. No market price is supplied.
expected: State the decision question, then write ad revenue as volume x share x paid clicks per unit x cost per click. Check that the reported click and price changes reproduce reported growth in each year before forecasting.

Reconcile falling share with record query growth by solving for the total-market growth that makes both true, and label it a calculation on an external estimate with its error. Prefer the direction of the panel series over its level.

Give each material driver an anchor class, reported history beside the value, a counter-argument, confidence, a two-sided shock range with its reason and a public observable or 'none'. Rank the drivers by output effect, report a joint stress, compare the first forecast year with the latest run-rate and with consensus without fitting to consensus, give the small flat line one rate, and name what is not modeled.
Do not call the result decision-grade while material drivers rest on an external estimate. Do not store the panel value in a reported series.
cases.held_out_request: Model SYNADS revenue out to 2036. I want to see what has to be true, not a single growth rate.

cases.request: What operating margin should the model use for SYNCO's core segment?
evidence: Synthetic 10-K K4, segment note: group operating margin 40.7%. The issuer discloses no margin for the core segment or for its video segment.

Video segment pays 55% of ad revenue to creators under published contract terms (synthetic terms page T1). Synthetic analog issuer ANALOG reports R&D and overhead at 18% of revenue. An independent analyst estimate E1 (2026-03-01) puts the video margin at 16%.
A KPI definition for core paid clicks exists in the store, with zero facts. The 10-K table that contains the value is in the document store.
expected: Estimate the other segments first, back out the core margin as the remainder, and label it a residual calculation with low confidence because it absorbs every other error.
Use the contractual payout as a bound on the video margin path, use the analog as an external estimate with the reason it fits, and cross-check against E1. Report a gap; do not tune to remove it.
Report the capture gap for paid clicks and its owner. A direct read of the filing can continue the analysis, stated as not passed through the resolver, and the output is not decision-grade.
Do not extend recent margin expansion when the growth forecast slows.
